messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xxs for /v1/generate (us-west-1). 5m error rate = 18% (threshold 3%). Paging oncall: @maria.garcia. Links: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/5678

maria.garcia: acked, joining bridge. reading dashboards now.

raj.patel: joining. I’m seeing a concurrent increase in p99 latency and queued requests on the inference pool.

emily: I pushed a small model-config tweak 12m ago to enable aggressive KV cache warming. rolling back now to test.

maria.garcia: thanks @emily — please paste the revert command when done. Also can someone check the autoscaler?

emily: reverted: ``kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-pool -n prod --to-revision=42``. rolling out.

ops-bot: deploy event: inference-pool rollback started by emily at 1870001159.

raj.patel: autoscaler is spiking because of a small task stuck in pre-warm, causing burst allocation attempts. Killing the stuck job cleared a backlog.

maria.garcia: ok after rollback + kill backlog, error rate dropped to ~6% but still above SLO. Any customer visible errors? product_ops, can you check top affected orgs?

product_ops: pinging CS for quick customer impact. early data: 3 orgs hit repeated 502s, highest affected is org_7632 (internal account). Not seeing broad billing-impact spikes.

naomi: I pulled request logs — most 502s correlate with kernel timeout on GPU node 5. That node was respecting probe, but slow nvlink reported.

sre_lead_jordan: proposal: evacuate traffic from node 5, mark node unschedulable, and run hardware healthcheck. If hardware noisy, cordon + taint and spin new nodes.

maria.garcia: done: cordoned node-5 and redirected 20% traffic to fallback model variant in us-east for high-priority customers.

raj.patel: traffic re-route looks stable; 5xxs now ~1.4% and latency normalized for most routes. Good catch on node 5.

incident-bot: bridge closed by oncall after mitigation at 1870001290. Final status: degraded -> mitigated.

maria.garcia: summary: root cause appears to be an interaction between the KV cache warming config and a flaky NVLink on node-5. The revert + node evacuation mitigated. Customer impact limited to a handful of orgs; we routed high-value orgs to fallback to protect SLAs.

emily: action items I’m tracking: 1) add a canary step to KV cache rollout (owner: emily) 2) add pre-deploy health check for nvlink stats (owner: infra-hw). I’ll file the tickets.

raj.patel: ops actions: 1) mark node-5 for hardware replacement (owner: raj) 2) add auto-evacuation rule if NVLink errors > 5 in 5m (owner: sre_lead_jordan).

naomi: monitoring follow-ups: 1) alert refinement for /v1/generate to separate 5xx type (gateway vs model) (owner: naomi) 2) add a temporary suppression window for autoscaler noise during small rollouts (owner: raj).

sre_lead_jordan: we need a postmortem and follow-through. propose scheduling a 60m blameless postmortem tomorrow at 16:00 UTC. attendees: oncall, infra-hw, runtime, product-ops.

product_ops: that time works for CS/PM to join. Please include incident timeline with customer hits.

maria.garcia: assigning owners and creating tickets now. Quick check: do we want to lower sensitivity of the primary alert or instead add multi-signal gating? I prefer gating (latency + error-type) to avoid flapping pages.

naomi: agree — gating is safer. Example rule idea: require 5m error_rate>3% AND p99>1s OR 2+ failed nodes contributing >20% requests. We should also add a suppression policy for rollout windows.

emily: sample alert snippet for gating I put together: ```
alert: GenerateHighError
expr: (
  avg_over_time(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",status=~"5.."}[5m])[5m:1m]) > 0.03
) and (
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le)) > 1
)
for: 5m
annotations:
  severity: "page"
  runbook: "https://wiki.redwood/alerts/generate_high_error"
```

maria.garcia: nice. For rollout suppression we can add an alertmanager inhibit rule or a temporary silence when a deploy event with tag `kv-warm` is in progress. ops-bot, can you auto-silence during recognized small rollouts?

ops-bot: I can. Need a config PR to allow pattern `kv-warm` in deploy metadata. Creating task: OPS-8234.

raj.patel: can we also add a simple exponential backoff for autoscaler when the node provisioning rate exceeds X? Current flapping makes things worse.

sre_lead_jordan: agree, add a guard in autoscaler: limit scale-up to +25% per 3m per pool. I'll open a ticket.

maria.garcia: postmortem plan: - owner: maria.garcia - doc: create page and timeline - include root cause analysis and customer impact - track action items into JIRA with owners and due dates - follow-up review in 2 weeks to verify fixes

maria.garcia: immediate action items I created: JIRA-1245 add canary to KV cache rollouts (emily, due 2w), JIRA-1246 NVLink healthcheck + auto-evacuate (raj, due 1w), JIRA-1247 Alert gating and suppression rules (naomi + jordan, due 1w), JIRA-1248 Autoscaler backoff (sre_lead_jordan, due 1w), JIRA-1249 Postmortem doc (maria.garcia, due 48h).

product_ops: noted. CS will follow up individually with org_7632 and the other affected customers.

naomi: I'll follow up on metrics dashboards to ensure the new split of 5xx types is visible on the primary oncall panel.

emily: I’ll add the canary step to the deploy pipeline doc and include a checklist for cache-related rollouts.

maria.garcia: thanks everyone. Closing thread for now — postmortem invite sent for 16:00 UTC tomorrow. Please add any additional notes to the doc before the meeting. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: postmortem scheduled: 60m, 1870088400 (tomorrow 16:00 UTC). Participants: maria.garcia, raj.patel, emily, naomi, sre_lead_jordan, product_ops.

maria.garcia: tagging follow-up owners — I’ll update this thread with links to the JIRA tickets and the postmortem doc once created.

naomi: small note for PMs — consider adding "fallback routing" as a documented mitigation option in the SLA playbook.

sre_lead_jordan: appreciated. I’ll add postmortem action tracker to the SRE OKR board so we get visibility.

maria.garcia: end of thread.
